channel.description: Latest articles from News Talk 980 CKNW (cknw.com)

item.title: LeBlanc says he’ll meet with Trump’s trade rep to talk about CUSMA review
item.description: LeBlanc said Ottawa and their Mexican counterparts are in agreement that a North American deal involving all three countries is the best way forward.

item.title: Promised replacement of aging long-term care home in Kelowna put on hold indefinitely
item.description: The news comes a year and half after former health minister Adrian Dix announced the much-needed replacement, saying then it was long overdue.

item.title: Katlim Desjarlais-Kelly found guilty of manslaughter in jury trial
item.description: Katlim Desjarlais-Kelly has been found guilty of manslaughter in the killing of 48-year-old Arden Panipekeseick in the Caswell Hill neighbourhood on Feb. 10, 2024.

item.title: $10-a-day daycare program paused in order to stabilize, B.C. government says
item.description: The province says the goal is to stabilize the program, instead of rolling it back and moving to income-tested eligibility. It was announced in the budget on Tuesday.

item.title: Overdoses tripled at Saskatoon supervised consumption site in 2025
item.description: Prairie Harm Reduction says it has also supported 22 per cent more people over the past year and successfully performed more than 150 interventions.

item.title: Métis elders in Saskatchewan celebrate launch of book featuring their stories
item.description: The stories of 12 Métis elders in Saskatchewan are being shared in a first-of-its-kind book published by Métis Nation—Saskatchewan.

item.title: RCMP investigating after fraudulent QR codes found on 75 Kelowna parking meters
item.description: City of Kelowna officials say the QR codes were not authorized by either the municipality or its mobile payment provider, PayByPhone.

item.title: After tragedy, Lapu Lapu victims were victims of ‘snooping’ at hospitals: report
item.description: In the aftermath of the deadly Lapu Lapu tragedy last April, dozens of people were rushed to hospitals to receive care, but some were victims of snooping.

item.title: Quebec hair salon ordered to pay $500 to non-binary client
item.description: A recent ruling from the Quebec human rights tribunal has put Station10 hair salon at the centre of a larger legal battle and social debate.
